[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Data-at-Rest Encryption in MySQL: Tablespaces and Redo/Undo Logs"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Data-at-Rest Encryption in MySQL protects physical storage (disks and backups) against unauthorized access. MySQL uses a two-tier key architecture: a Master Encryption Key (managed by a keyring plugin) and Tablespace/Log Encryption Keys."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Keyring Setup"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before enabling encryption, you must load a keyring plugin. MySQL provides several keyring plugins, such as keyring_file and keyring_encrypted_file. Below is the configuration to load the file-based keyring plugin in your my.cnf or my.ini file."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"early-plugin-load=keyring_file.so
keyring_file_data=/var/lib/mysql-keyring/keyring"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Encrypting General Tablespaces"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can encrypt individual tables when creating them by specifying the ENCRYPTION clause. This ensures that the physical pages written to disk for that table are fully encrypted."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE secured_data (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    sensitive_info VARCHAR(255)
) ENGINE=InnoDB ENCRYPTION="Y";"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can also alter an existing table to enable or disable encryption, provided the default encryption setting permits it."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"ALTER TABLE secured_data ENCRYPTION="Y";"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Encrypting Redo and Undo Logs"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Securing tablespaces is insufficient if unencrypted data leaks into transaction logs (Redo and Undo logs). You must explicitly enable log encryption to ensure complete data-at-rest security."},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"To enable Redo Log encryption, modify the global variable innodb_redo_log_encrypt:"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"SET GLOBAL innodb_redo_log_encrypt = ON;"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"To enable Undo Log encryption, modify the global variable innodb_undo_log_encrypt:"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"SET GLOBAL innodb_undo_log_encrypt = ON;"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Verifying Encryption Status"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can verify whether your tablespaces, redo logs, and undo logs are properly encrypted by querying the Performance Schema tables."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"SELECT NAME, ENCRYPTION FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.INNODB_TABLESPACES WHERE NAME LIKE "%secured_data%";"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Check redo log encryption via: SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES LIKE "innodb_redo_log_encrypt";"},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Check undo log encryption via: SHOW GLOBAL VARIABLES LIKE "innodb_undo_log_encrypt";"},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always backup your keyring file securely. Losing the keyring means permanent loss of access to your encrypted tablespaces and logs."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Rotate your master encryption key regularly using ALTER INSTANCE ROTATE InnoDB MASTER KEY."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Consider using enterprise keyring solutions like HashiCorp Vault or AWS Key Management Service (KMS) for production deployments."}]
